correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed from frozen RESULT.md: for r!=s the shorter source is an actual contiguous factor of the longer. In equal powers, U and V are contiguous overlaps in both; a common subsequence not embedding in U must use initial A of X and final A of Y, so it embeds in X with final B removed, namely V. Multiplicity of letters in each disjoint alphabet proves U and V incomparable. Exact lengths and all-positive-integer boundaries follow. Independently implemented scattered subsequence generation and one-character insertion maximality for 108 small disjoint-block/r/s cases, all matching. Tests are diagnostic; proof is general.
residual_risks: An embedding argument beyond the stated disjoint-alphabet hypothesis is invalid; overlapping example in source confirms necessity.

final_claim: For any nonempty disjoint-alphabet words A,B and r,s>=1, unequal powers have the shorter source itself as the unique maximal common scattered subsequence; at r=s=k exactly the two incomparable overlap words B(AB)^(k-1) and A(BA)^(k-1) generate the entire common-subsequence downward language; length gap ||A|-|B||.
limitations: No overlapping alphabets or cyclic alignment; counted distinct strings rather than embeddings.
